questions.question: What are variables in Robot Framework used for? (Select all that apply)

options.text: To store values that can be referenced and reused
To reduce hardcoding in multiple locations

options.explanation: Variables are for data management, not performance

questions.question: What are the five relevant ways to create and assign variables in Robot Framework? (Select all that apply)

options.explanation: Variables aren't compiled; they're defined or assigned

questions.question: What are the three attributes that define a variable in Robot Framework?

options.text: Prefix: $, @, &, or % to define access type
Delimiter: {} to enclose the variable name
Variable Name: the string that addresses the variable
Data Type: int, str, list, etc.
options.explanation: Data type is not a syntactical attribute; it's determined by the value

questions.question: What are the four syntactical access types for variables in Robot Framework?

options.explanation: There is no # prefix for constants

questions.question: How are variable names treated in Robot Framework?

options.text: Single spaces and underscores are ignored when matching
Unicode and special characters are allowed
Emojis can be used in variable names
Variable names must start with a letter
options.explanation: Variable names can start with any unicode character

questions.question: Which of these variable names refer to the same variable? (Select all that apply)

options.explanation: Different prefix (@) means different access type, not the same variable

questions.question: How do you use the literal text '${variable}' without it being interpreted as a variable?

options.explanation: Use backslash escaping, not doubling
Quotes become part of the value; use backslash

options.text: It cannot be used as literal text
options.explanation: Backslash escaping allows literal use

questions.question: What does the prefix in variable syntax define?

options.text: The access type to the variable
The data type stored in the variable
options.explanation: Prefix defines access type; actual data can be any type
Prefix is for access type; scope is defined elsewhere
Only % for environment variables are read-only

questions.question: When accessing a variable, which prefix is used in most cases?

options.explanation: @ is mainly for creation; $ is used for most access
& is mainly for creation; $ is used for most access

options.text: The same prefix used when creating it
options.explanation: $ is used for access in most cases regardless of creation prefix

questions.question: Where can variables be defined in the *** Variables *** section?

options.explanation: Library files use Python/Java, not *** Variables *** section
Variable files are a different concept

questions.question: What is the scope of variables defined in a suite file's *** Variables *** section?

options.text: Accessible throughout that specific suite to all tests/tasks and keywords
Only accessible in the first test case
options.explanation: Suite variables are accessible to all tests in the suite

options.text: Global to all suites in the project
options.explanation: Suite variables are suite-scoped, not global

options.text: Only accessible in the *** Variables *** section
options.explanation: Variables are meant to be used throughout the suite

questions.question: What is the scope of variables defined in a resource file's *** Variables *** section?

options.text: Accessible in all files that import the resource file directly or indirectly
Only accessible within the resource file itself
options.explanation: Resource file variables are shared with importing files
Only accessible to files that import the resource

options.text: Limited to the first importing file only
options.explanation: All importing files can access these variables

questions.question: When is the *** Variables *** section evaluated?

options.text: Before any other section in the resource or suite file

options.explanation: *** Variables *** is evaluated before other sections

options.text: When the variable is first used
options.explanation: The section is evaluated upfront, not lazily

options.text: At the end of file parsing
options.explanation: Variables are evaluated first

questions.question: What are the rules for creating variables in the *** Variables *** section? (Select all that apply)

options.text: Must be created as scalar ($), list-like (@), or dictionary-like (&)
Can use optional space and = for readability
Can be defined across multiple lines using ...
Must be indented like keyword calls
options.explanation: Variables in this section are not indented

questions.question: What is the recommended naming convention for variables in the *** Variables *** section?

options.text: UPPERCASE to distinguish from local variables

options.explanation: UPPERCASE is recommended for *** Variables *** section
UPPERCASE is the RF convention

options.text: Any case; there is no convention
options.explanation: UPPERCASE is the recommended convention

questions.question:
Analyze this variable definition:

```robot
*** Variables ***
${NAME}    Robot Framework
${VERSION}    8.0
${TOOL}    ${NAME}, version: ${VERSION}
```

What will ${TOOL} contain at runtime?

options.explanation: Variables are resolved at runtime

options.text: Error: cannot use variables in variable definitions
options.explanation: Variables can reference other variables
${NAME} resolves to 'Robot Framework', not 'TOOL'

questions.question: How are multiple-line scalar variable values joined by default?

options.explanation: Default is space; use separator= for no space
Default is space; use separator=\n for newlines
Default is space, not comma

questions.question:
Examine this variable definition:

```robot
*** Variables ***
${EXAMPLE}    This value is joined
...    together with a space.
```

What will ${EXAMPLE} contain?

options.text: This value is joined together with a space.
This value is joinedtogether with a space. (no space)
options.explanation: Default separator is space

options.text: This value is joined\ntogether with a space. (with newline)
options.explanation: Would need separator=\n for newline

options.text: Just the first line: 'This value is joined'
options.explanation: Both lines are joined

questions.question: How do you specify a custom separator for multi-line scalar variables?

options.text: Add separator=<value> as the last value

options.explanation: Use separator=<value> in the variable definition

options.text: Put the separator in square brackets
options.explanation: Use separator=<value> syntax
Custom separators are supported with separator=

questions.question:
Analyze this variable:

```robot
*** Variables ***
${URL}    https://example.com/search
...    ?query=robot+framework
...    &page=1
...    separator=
```

What will ${URL} contain?

options.explanation: separator= means no separator
All lines are joined with separator=
Empty separator is valid

questions.question: What are the primitive data types supported in Robot Framework syntax? (Select all that apply)

options.explanation: Chars are just strings of length 1

questions.question: How are non-string primitive data types defined?

options.explanation: Use scalar syntax ${42}, not special prefixes
Quotes make it a string; use ${42}
No type declarations needed; use ${42}

questions.question:
Analyze these variable definitions:

```robot
*** Variables ***
${STRING}    This is a string
${STILL_STRING}    8270
${INTEGER}    ${42}
${ANSWER}    The answer is ${INTEGER}
```

What will ${ANSWER} contain?

options.text: The answer is 42 (integer converted to string)

options.explanation: Variables are resolved and types converted

options.text: Error: cannot concatenate string and integer
options.explanation: Integer is automatically converted to string
${INTEGER} resolves to its value 42

questions.question: How do you define a list variable in the *** Variables *** section?

options.text: Using @{variable_name} followed by values separated by multiple spaces

options.explanation: Use @ prefix, not $ with brackets
Use @ prefix, not LIST keyword

options.text: Lists cannot be defined in *** Variables *** section
options.explanation: Lists can be defined using @ syntax

questions.question:
Examine this list variable:

```robot
*** Variables ***
@{NAMES}    Matti    Teppo
@{NUMBERS}    one    two    three
...    four    five    six
```

How do you access the value 'Teppo'?

options.explanation: Use $ for accessing individual items, not @
Index starts at 0; 'Matti' is [0], 'Teppo' is [1]
Use square brackets [1], not dot notation

questions.question: How do you define a dictionary variable in the *** Variables *** section?

options.explanation: Use & prefix with key=value syntax
Use & prefix, not DICT keyword

options.text: Dictionaries cannot be defined in *** Variables *** section
options.explanation: Dictionaries can be defined using & syntax

questions.question:
Examine this dictionary variable:

```robot
*** Variables ***
&{USER1}    name=Matti    address=xxx    phone=123
&{USER2}    name=Teppo    address=yyy    phone=456
```

How do you access the name from USER1?

options.explanation: Use $ for accessing values, not &
Quotes are not needed around keys

questions.question: How do you escape an equal sign in a dictionary key?

options.explanation: Use backslash escaping, not doubling
Quotes become part of the key; use backslash

options.text: Equal signs cannot be in keys
options.explanation: They can with escaping

questions.question: What special features do dictionaries created with &{} syntax have? (Select all that apply)

options.explanation: Dictionaries can be modified

questions.question:
How can you dynamically access a dictionary value using a variable for the key?

```robot
${key}    Set Variable    phone
# Access USER1's phone
```

options.explanation: Attribute access doesn't support variable keys
This would look for literal 'key', not the variable's value
Use $ for accessing, not &

questions.question: How do you assign a return value from a keyword to a variable?

options.text: Variable name with optional =, then keyword call
Keyword call, then arrow →, then variable name
options.explanation: RF uses variable = keyword syntax
RETURN is in the keyword; assignment is in the caller
This is a primary way to use variables

questions.question:
Analyze this example:

```robot
*** Settings ***
Library    OperatingSystem

*** Test Cases ***
Example
    ${server_log} =    Get File    server.log
    Should Contain    ${server_log}    Success
```

What is the scope of ${server_log}?

options.explanation: Variables from return values are local by default
Return value assignments create local variables

options.text: Available only in the Get File keyword
options.explanation: The variable is in the test, not the keyword

questions.question: If a keyword returns multiple values to a scalar variable, how are they stored?

options.text: As a list of values accessible with index syntax
Only the first value is stored
options.explanation: All values are stored as a list
Values remain as a list, not concatenated
Single scalar variable can hold multiple values as a list

questions.question:
Examine this code:

```robot
*** Settings ***
Library    OperatingSystem

*** Test Cases ***
Example
    ${path}    ${file} =    Split Path    server/logs/server.log
    Should Be Equal    ${path}    server/logs
    Should Be Equal    ${file}    server.log
```

What is happening in the Split Path line?

options.text: Two return values assigned to two separate scalar variables
Two arguments passed to Split Path
options.explanation: server/logs/server.log is the argument; ${path} and ${file} receive returns

options.text: Creating a list with two elements
options.explanation: Creating two separate variables, not one list

options.text: Syntax error: cannot assign to two variables
options.explanation: Multiple assignment is valid

questions.question: What is the VAR statement used for?

options.text: To create and assign variables within test/task or keyword bodies during execution
To define variables in the *** Variables *** section
options.explanation: VAR is for inline definition in test/keyword bodies
VAR creates variables, not declares types
VAR creates mutable variables

options.text: VAR can create dictionary variables using &{}
Variables created by VAR have suite scope
options.explanation: VAR creates local scope by default

questions.question: What are common use cases for the VAR statement? (Select all that apply)

options.text: Conditional assignments based on runtime conditions
Initializing variables (like empty lists before FOR loops)

options.explanation: Use *** Variables *** section for suite-level constants

questions.question: What is the default scope of variables created with VAR statement?

options.text: Local to the test/task or keyword where defined

options.explanation: VAR creates local scope by default
VAR creates local scope unless scope= is specified
Default is local; use scope= to change

questions.question: What are the two main variable scopes introduced in this chapter?

options.text: LOCAL scope - variables created within test/task or keyword
SUITE scope - variables defined in *** Variables *** section

options.explanation: GLOBAL scope is mentioned but details are in chapter 5
TEST scope details are in chapter 5

questions.question: Which statements about LOCAL scope variables are correct? (Select all that apply)

options.text: Created by keyword return value assignment
Cannot be accessed outside their block
Are destroyed when the block completes
Can be accessed from called keywords automatically
options.explanation: LOCAL variables cannot be accessed in called keywords unless passed as arguments
